scope: X-M1 1.50 shared owned detection-output provider for task100, actuators and task99, source-only

canonical_core.boundary: DetectionOutputBackend with ServiceStatus failures; owned fields are read and written through the canonical DetectionField enum; physical source numbers come from DetectionMode::irq_source

provenance.source_class: NONMATCHING functions, canonical implementation records byte confirmation
provenance.byte_confirmation: Canonical evidence identifies id4.dis:159594-159825 for mode and callback functions, id4.dis:160483-160496 for clock initialization

implementation.initialization: DetectionState::new starts uninitialized; initialize invokes the canonical initializer before admitting registration
implementation.callback: Canonical DetectionCallback is a typed callback generation, never a code address. Closed recipient routing selects EepromEvents DMA signal, actual ActuatorEvents atomic mailbox, or actual task99 ControlSender queue posting
implementation.register_boundary: DetectionRegister and LensDmaRegister select volatile physical MMIO only; no retained 0x91a548 state reads or writes
implementation.native_ownership: NativeDetectionContext owns one state, IO, EepromEvents, ActuatorEvents and Task99DetectionEvents. bind accepts a permanent shared reference, initializes canonical fields under the IRQ lock, and installs one AtomicPtr context. Fixed owned handlers select the stored owner and dispatch into this context; no mutable singleton reference or stock callback address is retained
implementation.borrow_boundary: Provider holds shared references, enters the physical critical section before borrowing owned state, drops the mutable state borrow before event delivery, and leaves the outer critical section after delivery
implementation.failure_cleanup: Cancellation clears only the caller's event recipient. A stale recipient cannot detach another owner's active IRQ. Failed release restores the owned handle for cleanup retry. Failed attachment clears the active generation and unregisters canonical callback state
implementation.task99_power: Task99DetectionPower implements actual ControlPower mode and callback registration through the same canonical provider. Callback IDs use the closed 0x30000000..0x3fffffff namespace and are never reused
implementation.task99_delivery: Task99DetectionEvents binds an actual permanent ControlSender. Off completion posts Poll/DeviceCompletion DetectionOff; On and Probe post DetectionOn, with SUCCESS and sixteen zero bytes. It does not post Ready or BeginDetection directly
implementation.task99_failures: ControlSender posting failures remain observable through events.take_failure as ControlError. Canonical and registration failures remain observable through power.take_failure as ServiceStatus

integration.native_constructor: NativeDetectionContext::new(EepromEvents), followed by bind on a static context. Existing EEPROM provider/events accessors remain unchanged; actuator_provider/actuator_events and task99_provider/task99_power/task99_events share that same context
integration.dma_registration: Caller reserves the unique EepromEvents DMA callback before register_dma_callback(Some(callback)); canonical continuous low detection owns the physical attachment
integration.dma_cancellation: Provider cancel and registration of None call EepromEvents::cancel_dma and unregister the canonical callback. Future cancellation must invoke provider.cancel even if event cancellation already occurred
integration.actuator_registration: DetectionProvider::for_actuator(state,io,ActuatorEvents) uses the concrete lens_actuator_cpu mailbox, whose implementation is supplied by actuator commit 5f8abe30
integration.task99_registration: Bind task99_events to the actual permanent ControlSender, then pass task99_power to the owned task99 ControlDevice. Every registration first cancels the previous task99 registration and then arms its next typed callback
integration.startup_caller: Actual 6b8f78 startup must call canonical provider initialization or native context.bind, not retain the old physical-clock-only helper. LensComposition owns this caller integration
integration.event_synchronization: Every ARM EepromEvents RefCell access must be protected by the same physical IRQ lock; parent provider owns this protection
integration.irq_kernel: Root supplies owned IRQ exports backed by the shared charge_timers handle registry and rtos_irq_control executor, not retained firmware entrypoints

behavioral_tests_authored: Uninitialized provider neither attaches nor completes
Initializer programs both clocks and low DMA waits for a qualified IRQ
Input transition during qualification does not complete DMA
Cancellation and rearm reject stale typed callback generations and wrong sources
One-shot high and probe modes attach the appropriate physical source
Attachment failures preserve status and invalidate the callback
Detachment failures suppress callbacks and retain cleanup capability
DMA register writes reach the physical IO boundary
Shared actuator and EEPROM owners route physical callbacks separately, including colliding numeric IDs
Stale actuator or EEPROM cancellation preserves the other owner's active physical registration
Canonical set_mode cancellation and enabled-mode immediate completion remain observable
Task99 physical callbacks post the actual internal DeviceCompletion message before actor transitions
Task99 cancellation rejects old generations and cannot detach active actuator registration
Task99 queue failures remain observable without synthesizing an actor transition
verification: No builds, tests, lint, formatting, native execution, SDK execution or camera operations performed. Authored tests are unexecuted. No runtime qualification or camera readiness is claimed.
